definition: Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36–51) are non-justiciable guidelines for governance toward a welfare state. They complement Fundamental Rights and inform legislative and policy choices; courts may use DPSPs for interpretation and proportionality.

statutoryReferences.note: Cross-read with Fundamental Rights (Part III) for exam answers

examChecklist.text: Distinguish DPSPs from Fundamental Rights (enforceability, nature)
Give examples of DPSPs and corresponding legislative steps
